turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I’m here because I’m having a hard time keeping all the moving parts organized. I’ve got patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions… and instead of doing what actually matters, I end up just starting with whatever feels loudest or most urgent in the moment. It’s gotten to the point where I don’t feel like I can manage it the way I used to.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly reports difficulty organizing multiple responsibilities and prioritizing what matters.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself having trouble focusing on a single task for an extended period of time?
turns.patient_response: Yes. If I’m coding and something interrupts me, even something small like a Slack ping or a tab flashing, I can completely lose the thread. Sometimes just a visual idea pops into my head and I’ll end up going down some unrelated design rabbit hole for twenty minutes before I realize I’m not doing the original task anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient reports being distracted by Slack pings, flashing tabs, and unrelated thoughts, causing them to lose track of coding tasks for extended periods.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed when you're having trouble focusing or getting interrupted?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’d call it anxious exactly. It’s more that I get frustrated and kind of overloaded when I can’t get back to what I was doing. Like I know there was a thread there, but I can’t grab it again.

symptom_reasoning.S059: The patient describes becoming overloaded and being unable to regain their train of thought after an interruption, consistent with difficulty concentrating.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Mostly on long design calls. If I’m sitting there too long, I feel this pressure building up to move, so I’ll start shifting around or switch chairs. Sometimes I just get up and pace around my office while I’m still trying to look like I’m paying attention.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient endorses a building pressure to move during prolonged sitting and sometimes gets up to pace.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient reports shifting around and switching chairs while sitting, consistent with fidgety or squirming behavior.

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience these difficulties with focus and restlessness at home or when you're not working, as well?
turns.patient_response: Yes, it happens at home too. After I’ve worked late, I’ll try to sit quietly or read something non-work-related to wind down, but after a few minutes I’m tapping my fingers, checking my phone, or getting up to adjust something around the room. I don’t really settle into it.

symptom_reasoning.S013: At home, the patient cannot settle into quiet reading or winding down and repeatedly gets up or checks their phone.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient reports tapping their fingers while trying to sit quietly.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a kid?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, looking back, it was there in grade school. Teachers would say I was bright, but I daydreamed a lot. I’d finish assignments and then forget to turn them in, or I’d lose my homework folder. That was happening well before I was a teenager.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient reports frequent daydreaming in grade school, indicating difficulty sustaining attention.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient reports losing homework folders needed for schoolwork.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient reports forgetting to turn in completed assignments.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking or blurt out answers before they've finished asking a question?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think that’s a big issue for me. I mean, I might occasionally jump in if I’m excited or think I know where someone’s going, but I haven’t really noticed myself constantly interrupting people or blurting things out.

symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient denies frequently blurting out answers, noting this occurs only occasionally.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient denies constant interrupting, describing only occasional interjections when excited or anticipating where someone is going.

turns.doctor_question: Have your difficulties with focus, restlessness, or organization ever caused problems in your relationships or at work?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Work is where it’s become the most obvious. It’s started to hurt how people see me there. I missed a checkpoint for a patent filing, which was a big deal, and after a tough architecture review, some of the people I work with seemed to question whether I could really lead the larger project. That was hard to hear, but I understand why they’d be concerned.

symptom_reasoning.functional_impairment: The patient reports work-related consequences, including missing a patent filing checkpoint and colleagues questioning their ability to lead a larger project.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and restlessness consistently throughout your adult life?
turns.patient_response: Not really consistently my whole adult life, no. I mean, I’ve had some tendencies before, but it became a real problem about a year or so ago—maybe a year and a month—after that award pushed me into leading more coordination-heavy work. Since then it’s been much harder to manage.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever experienced periods where your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity were absent or much less noticeable?
turns.patient_response: Yes, before about a year ago it was much less noticeable. It’s really been a problem for about a year and a month now, after that award led to me taking on more coordination-heavy work. Since then, it’s been harder to ignore.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that your difficulties with focus, restlessness, and organization are causing you significant distress?
turns.patient_response: Yes, it is. I’m pretty worried about what it’s doing to my reputation at work. Missing that patent filing checkpoint was embarrassing and had real consequences, and after the architecture review, I could tell some collaborators were questioning whether I’m able to lead the bigger project. That’s been weighing on me a lot.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient reports significant distress and occupational consequences related to focus, restlessness, and organization difficulties, including damage to work reputation and concern about leadership capacity.

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience these difficulties with focus and restlessness when you're on vacation or completely away from work and other responsibilities?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to it when I’m fully away from work. On vacation I’m usually not tracking it the same way, so I can’t say clearly whether it’s still there or not.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your difficulties with focus and restlessness happen when you're doing things you enjoy, like hobbies?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think so. Even when I’m trying to do something I want to enjoy, like reading something nontechnical after working late, I don’t really settle into it. After a few minutes I’ll be tapping, checking my phone, or getting up to adjust something instead of actually winding down.

symptom_reasoning.S013: Even during an enjoyable leisure activity, the patient cannot settle quietly and repeatedly gets up instead of winding down.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient reports tapping after only a few minutes of trying to read.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your difficulties with focus and restlessness mostly happen in situations where there's a lot of structure or expectation, like at work, or can they also occur in more unstructured or relaxed settings?
turns.patient_response: It can happen in relaxed settings too. Like after working late, I’ll try to just sit quietly or read something nontechnical, and within a few minutes I’m tapping, checking my phone, or getting up to adjust something. So it’s not only when there’s a work deadline or a lot of structure.

symptom_reasoning.S013: The patient reports being unable to remain settled while trying to sit quietly or read in a relaxed setting, instead checking their phone or getting up within minutes.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient explicitly reports tapping while attempting to relax.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think your difficulties with focus and restlessness would improve if your work demands and responsibilities were significantly reduced?
turns.patient_response: Maybe somewhat, but I don’t think it would fully go away. What really pushed me to come in is that I can’t organize all the moving parts anymore—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions. Even if the workload were lighter, I feel like I’d still end up jumping to whatever feels most urgent or loudest instead of what actually matters.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly reports being unable to organize multiple work-related tasks and responsibilities, and prioritizing whichever demand feels most urgent rather than what matters most.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced significant difficulties with focus, restlessness, or organization for at least 6 months?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It’s been more than six months — about a year and a month now. It really became a problem after the award pushed me into leading more coordination-heavy work. Since then the focus and organization issues have been pretty consistent.

turns.doctor_question: Have your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity been present for most days over the past year?
turns.patient_response: Yes, most days. It’s been a real problem for about a year and a month now, since that award pushed me into more coordination-heavy work. It hasn’t really just come and gone — it’s been pretty steady.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and restlessness for most of your adult life before the past year?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I can’t say I’ve had this at the same level for most of my adult life. Before the past year, I don’t think I noticed it as a major problem like this.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have any notable symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity during your childhood or adolescence that were not as noticeable until recently?
turns.patient_response: Yes, looking back, I think there were signs in grade school. Teachers would say I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I also remember forgetting to turn in assignments even when I’d finished them, and losing homework folders. That was happening well before I was a teenager.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient reports that teachers said they daydreamed a lot in grade school, supporting childhood attention difficulty.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient recalls forgetting to turn in assignments despite having completed them, indicating failure to follow through with school-related duties.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient reports losing homework folders during grade school.
